controls_available: Difficulty 1 uses exact shortest-path scramble depth 2.

Full interaction exposes three brass disc handles (north, southwest, southeast); dragging a handle at least 0.45 radians requests one clockwise or counter-clockwise sixth-turn, with input_source rim_drag.
A legal turn synchronously rotates the selected disc on pointerup; an illegal turn is synchronously refused and leaves the rose unchanged.
SEAL submits the event transcript; RETRY is available only after a failed submission and rerenders a fresh challenge. Both are agent-triggered, with certification administrative.
The configured real-time settings are play_time_seconds=180, observation_window_ms=0, and frames_per_observation=1.
autonomous_processes: None between agent actions. Handle preview movement occurs only during the agent's pointermove sequence, and rose state changes only inside the agent-triggered turn attempt on pointerup. Submission feedback is asynchronous UI feedback after an agent-triggered administrative action, not autonomous task-state evolution.
grouped_control_modes: D = all outcome-affecting full-mode rim_drag turn attempts across the three discs and both directions; certification and retry are not autonomous outcome controls.

clause_i.reason: For the rim_drag family, prior actions alone cannot choose the optimal first turn across the generated depth-2 states: the generator samples multiple eligible states and their shortest solution moves differ.

clause_ii.reason: A current screenshot contains the reference arrangement, current rose, disc geometry, and visible handles, so a bounded static visual policy can select a legal optimal turn; no temporal window is needed.

clause_iii.reason: For every positive delay during a solvable rim_drag opportunity, supplying no new action leaves the rose state, legal-turn outcome, and visible task content unchanged. The source contains no timer, animation, physics tick, or frame-driven state update. Therefore the action value and its advantage over no-op do not strictly decrease; any lost wall-clock deadline is explicitly excluded by the definition.

common_visible_process: None. No autonomous visible process is shared by the control opportunities, so no common D, positive Delta, and bounded window can satisfy all three clauses.

pre_run.reason: The mathematical definition already yields No because clause (iii) fails; there is no autonomous outcome phase whose pre-run rate could override that result.

source_evidence.claim: The requested difficulty-1 profile is very_easy with scramble_depth 2.
Full mode is brass-handle rim dragging, and the configured observation window is 0 ms with one frame.
The task is a three-disc visual puzzle; runner settings use a zero-ms observation window and synchronous execution.
Legal turns and sixth-turn state updates are pure state transformations with no timing or autonomous update.
The generator builds a finite static BFS graph from the solved state.
The difficulty control condition supplies scramble_depth, samples a depth frontier by seed, and exports the visible rose plus solution contract; no future process is generated.
Full mode omits proxy buttons; each turn is evaluated and applied synchronously in attempt, with illegal turns refused.
The only handle movement is directly driven by pointerdown/pointermove/pointerup, and attempt runs only after the agent completes a drag.
Retry and submission are agent-triggered actions; the only asynchronous operation is the administrative result fetch.
Rendering installs only pointer, certify, and retry event listeners; there is no timer, animation loop, or autonomous state handler.
The relevant CSS supplies static layout and drag cursor styling without a task-state animation or keyframe process.
The grader binds full interaction to rim_drag and replays only the submitted discrete event transcript and bandaged-disc physics.
The verifier independently replays the event list, checks the interaction source, and determines completion from the final static state.
The shared verifier helper only loads the exported result from the task container; it adds no task-time evolution.
The full-mode scripted solver performs direct handle drags for each discrete solution move, with optional delays only in the solver's own pointer sequence.
The solver waits for each synchronous successful-turn counter update, then certifies; it does not rely on an autonomous outcome phase.
The frozen definition requires strict action-value loss from non-clock autonomous task-state evolution, visibly evidenced by the same process.
A static puzzle with no changing task state fails the real-time conjunction even if wall-clock or deadline progression exists.
